subject: RPO sampling request & keystore rotation artifacts
messages:
From: Lara Quinn <lara.quinn@clearwater.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@clearwater.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RPO sampling and keystore rotation — artifacts request

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our SOC2 readiness gate we need a short set of artifacts to close the RPO/RTO control: specifically a sampling of (1) a warm KV/cache snapshot near-production timestamped with checksums, (2) the keystore rotation event log around the last scheduled rotation, and (3) a short excerpt of the restore runbook showing the steps you would use to rehydrate a warm replica.

Can you provide a redacted sample bundle (logs/artifact manifest) and confirm whether you can HMAC-sign the manifest so we can verify chain-of-custody during our audit? If a live walk-through is easier, we can take that as an alternative (30–45 min).

Target dates: our external auditor is aiming to close this by Nov 10. Ideally we get artifacts by Oct 31 and schedule a live session first week of Nov if needed.

Questions:
- Can you confirm what you will redact (PII/tenant IDs) versus what we will see in full?
- Will the keystore rotation log include KMS audit event IDs?
- Do you have a checksum manifest we can validate?

Appreciate it — cc'ing compliance for tracking.

Best,
Lara
Lara Quinn
Sr. Risk Manager | ClearWater Financial

[Attachment: auditor-request-template.pdf (pdf)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lara Quinn <lara.quinn@clearwater.com>
Cc: compliance@clearwater.com, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RPO sampling and keystore rotation — artifacts request

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. We can do both: provide a redacted artifact bundle by Oct 31 and run a live 30–45 minute walk-through the week of Nov 1 (we have slots on Nov 2 or Nov 4).

Scope and what we'll provide:
- A timestamped KV/cache snapshot (sample subset) with a checksum file (sha256) and a signed manifest. Sensitive keys and tenant IDs will be redacted; we will preserve timestamps and object IDs so you can follow restore order.
- Keystore rotation log CSV with KMS event IDs and rotation metadata (we will mask full key material names but include rotation event IDs and audit timestamps).
- Restore runbook excerpt (PDF) with the exact steps we run for a warm restore, plus the minimal operator checklist.

We will HMAC-sign the manifest (access-manifest-hmac.sig) using a Redwood audit key and include instructions on verifying the signature. If your auditor needs an additional verification channel, we can add an S3 presigned file and a short video of the checksum verification.

Action items for me:
- Confirm redaction approach (do you want tenant names fully redacted or pseudo-IDs?)
- Reserve a live-walkthrough slot (Nov 2 or Nov 4)

Looping in Dev (ops) to confirm the exact filenames and the HMAC process.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lara Quinn <lara.quinn@clearwater.com>
Cc: compliance@clearwater.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RPO sampling and keystore rotation — artifacts request

Thanks Mina and Lara — quick technical note from Ops on the artifacts we'll hand over: 

What we'll include (filenames):
- rpo-snapshot-20271027.json (sampled keys/objects; timestamps preserved)
- kv-snapshot-checksum.txt (sha256 checksums for each object line-by-line)
- keystore-rotation-log-20271026.csv (rotation events with KMS event IDs; key names redacted to pseudo-IDs like redwood_k_XXXX)
- access-manifest-hmac.sig (HMAC-SHA256 of the manifest, key stored in our audit KMS)
- runbook-restore-excerpt.pdf (operator steps, validation checks)

Methodology / verification notes:
- Snapshots are taken from the warm cache replica; each object includes a monotonic timestamp and an internal object id. We will provide a pairing of object id -> pseudo-tenant id so auditors can follow sequence without seeing tenant names.
- The manifest will contain a UTC timestamp and a manifest_id. We will include an HMAC header with the algorithm and the KMS key ARN (redacted partial).
- For chain-of-custody we time-stamp the bundle and upload to a restricted shared Drive folder (link to follow) and keep a separate verification hash via our audit KMS.
- Keystore rotations are recorded in our central audit pipeline; rotation events include KMS event ids and change summaries. We cannot provide plaintext key material, but the event IDs and rotation diffs are sufficient for auditors to verify that rotation occurred and was recorded.

Operational ask: Mina, do you want me to include a short screencast of the checksum verification step? I can record it and place it in the Drive folder.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RPO sampling and keystore rotation — artifacts request

Hi Lara — attaching the sample bundle per our plan. We redacted tenant display names and replaced them with pseudo-IDs; timestamps, object IDs, and checksums are intact. The HMAC signature was produced with our audit key; verification instructions are in the README inside the Drive folder.

Attachments included: rpo-snapshot-20271027.json, kv-snapshot-checksum.txt, keystore-rotation-log-20271026.csv, access-manifest-hmac.sig, runbook-restore-excerpt.pdf

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cRedwood-RPO-SAMPLE-2027 (access restricted to invited auditor addresses).

Confirmed live-walkthrough: Nov 2 at 10:00 AM PT — Agenda: 1) artifact checksum verification (10 min) 2) walkthrough of keystore rotation log and KMS event IDs (10 min) 3) restore runbook rehearsal (15 min) 4) Q&A and next steps (10–15 min). Invite will follow.

If your auditor needs additional context (e.g., logs for a different rotation window or an expanded snapshot), let us know and we can provide a scoped addendum.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Trust Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
